headline: Approved two-lot subdivisions at 190 Hampstead Road and Worthley Road, with conditions, and $58,811 escrow for 57 Crystal Avenue.
summary: A Southern New Hampshire Planning Commission team presented results of a Derry housing readiness pilot study. The board approved a letter of credit release for 35 Maple Street. A workshop on zoning changes to match new state laws was moved to a later meeting.
decisions: Approved a cash escrow of $58,811 for the 57 Crystal Avenue site redevelopment, unanimously.
Approved release number two of a letter of credit for 35 Maple Street and a replacement letter of $30,721.68, unanimously.
Approved a waiver so the Knottensun subdivision lot size is set by lot area instead of soil size, 7-2.
Approved a waiver allowing Knottensun subdivision lot lines that are not substantially at right angles to the streets, unanimously.
Approved a waiver from the driveway sight distance profile requirement for the Knottensun subdivision, unanimously.
Approved a waiver from setting granite bounds where existing bounds cannot be removed by law, unanimously.
Approved the two-lot Knottensun subdivision on Worthley Road with conditions, 6-2.
Motion that the 190 Hampstead Road subdivision is a development of regional impact failed.
Approved the two-lot subdivision at 190 Hampstead Road with conditions, unanimously.
discussion: Housing pilot study: Members asked about downtown storefront rules, how zoning affects which housing types fit, and whether affordability depends on zoning alone.
Worthley Road driveway: Discussion focused on the steep grade, runoff from the new cut, and whether fire trucks could reach the lot.
Worthley Road access easement: Discussion covered whether construction could block an abutter's access, and whether the board has authority to set terms.
Hampstead Road drainage: Abutters worried that new roof and pavement could send more water toward their yards and Drew Woods.
Soil-based lot sizing waiver: Members debated whether a state test pit and subdivision approval were enough to skip soil-based lot sizing on a ledge-prone hill.
